Dividing by zero is the same as multiplying by 1/0.

If m and n are two nonzero integers, you can multiply m by n to get mn and then multiply mn by 1/n to get back m. If you multiply 5 by 0, you get 0. But if you multiply 7 by 0, you also get 0. If you multiply any number z, by 0, you get 0. So then what happens when you multiply 0 by 1/0? Do you get 5, 7 or any other number? There is no way of knowing what the initial number z was. It's a one way operation.

It's like if you have a bag of colored beads and one of those beads is on the table. You can see its color. Then you throw it in the bag with the rest.
